source_refs.note: 7. Torricelli's Theorem: a main subheading of 5.12 Uses of Bernoulli's principle, its own page (owner 2026-11-04); PDF 109-112.

blocks.text: A simple application of Bernoulli's equation is shown in Fig. 5.23. Suppose a large tank of fluid has two small orifices A and B on it, as shown in Fig. 5.23. Let us find the speed with which the water flows from the orifice A.

blocks.alt: A tall tank of water whose surface, moving down with speed v1, is at height h1 above the bottom. Orifice A on the right, at height h2 above the bottom and h1 - h2 below the surface, lets out a jet with speed v2 that curves down. Orifice B, low on the left, leads into a tube that turns the jet upward (speed v3), and the water rises to the level of the water in the tank.
blocks.caption: Figure 5.23: A tank containing fluid with a orifice (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 5.23).

blocks.text: Since the orifices are so small, the efflux speeds v₂ and v₃ will be much larger than the speed v₁ of the top surface of water. We can therefore, take v₁ as approximately zero. Hence, Bernoulli's equation can be written as:

blocks.latex: P_1 + \rho g h_1 = P_2 + \frac{1}{2}\rho v_2^2 + \rho g h_2

blocks.text: This is Torricelli's theorem which states that:
The speed of efflux is equal to the velocity gained by the fluid in falling through the distance (h₁ - h₂) under the action of gravity.
bold: The speed of efflux is equal to the velocity gained by the fluid in falling through the distance (h₁ - h₂) under the action of gravity.

blocks.text: Notice that the speed of the efflux of liquid is the same as the speed of a ball that falls through a height (h₁ - h₂). The top level of the tank has moved down a little and the P.E. has been transferred into K.E. of the efflux of fluid. If the orifice had been pointed upward at B as shown in Fig.6.4, this K.E. would allow the liquid to rise to the level of water tank. In practice, viscous-energy losses would alter the result to some extent.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Chapter 5 has no Fig. 6.4. The tank with orifices A and B, the tube at B turned upward, is Fig. 5.23.
